name: How do installers handle uneven ceilings and crooked corners?

mainEntity.name: How do installers handle uneven ceilings and crooked corners?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost no drywall ceiling or corner is perfectly square or flat, especially in older homes or settling framing. Finish carpenters handle this through scribing, backing blocks, and coped joints rather than simple miter cuts. A coped joint cuts the profile along the contour of the adjoining piece so the seam stays tight even when walls sit out of square. Minor gaps along wavy drywall are backed with shims, nailed into solid ceiling joists or wall studs, and finished with paintable acrylic caulk before final topcoats are applied.
acceptedAnswer.description: Installers cope inside corners, install solid backing, and scribe trim to match contours. Flexible caulk and careful fastening bridge minor ceiling variations cleanly.
